changes: Added a source-first process-fact registry contract: process-fact-registry.ts now centralizes command lifecycle facts, reviewer lanes, review/finding/validation evidence, and gate artifact metadata; verify-process-fact-contract.mjs verifies command policy, phase tools, process levels, signed artifacts, final registry composition, and mapped export wiring.
usage: Run npm run test:process-fact-contract to inspect and verify the unified Koala process-fact registry; run koala validate --channel --story=B-5964 to verify normal-channel execution evidence.
expectedOutcome: Maintainers can rely on one hard-coded registry/config-table contract for phase state, review pass, finding state, validation evidence, and gate artifacts; prompt text only guides behavior and cannot be the fallback.
actualTranscript: npm run test:process-fact-contract printed Process Fact Contract, listed 110 registry entries including 84 CLI facts, 10 reviewer lanes, and 13 artifacts, then ended with Process fact contract verified; koala validate --story=B-5964 --json passed with 12/12 verification intents covered.
outcomeDiff: No gap: expected centralized hard-coded process-fact contract is visible and mechanically verified; validation and channel gates pass.
limitations: none — fully covered by source-first contract verification, reviewer approval, and Koala validate.
pitfalls: Initial review exposed three important hardening gaps: artifact coverage was too narrow, dist output could hide source drift, and mapped registry exports were reconstructed instead of validated. Channel gate also required rewriting the local story branch so code commits are authored by koala-implementer.
